_note: The body (2026-11-13, rebuilt on a professional's figures; ADR-052 note: derived, never adjusted). Top speed: top_speed_min + (top_speed_max - top_speed_min) x max_speed. Acceleration: (accel_min + (accel_max - accel_min) x explosive_force) x weight_ref / weight, dimmed by fatigue (ADR-030: 1 - fatigue_coefficient x fatigue, floored). Braking: decel_min + (decel_max - decel_min) x body_control: he slows down to stop where he is going, and to turn. He moves in a straight line towards his target (before, a diagonal ran 1.4 times his top speed). His pace is his: when he contests something (pressing, going in, going for the ball, running in behind, carrying it) he runs as fast as he can; when he takes up his place he goes at the speed that gets him there in about reposition_ticks. Before, every player ran every run at full speed (13 km a match, a third of the time above 4 m/s). The characteristics are read through the range, never to zero (before, an average player reached 4.5 m/s, accelerating at 1.5 m/s2). With the ball (2026-11-13, plan L0-CLOSE 10a): his top speed is with_ball_share_min + (with_ball_share_max - with_ball_share_min) x dribbling of his sprint: the good dribbler runs almost as fast with it.
_source: Professional footballers' peak sprint speeds of about 7.5-10 m/s (27-36 km/h, top-league tracking data); maximal accelerations of about 2.5-5 m/s2 and decelerations larger than accelerations, up to 5-6 m/s2 and more (Harper, Carling and Kiely 2019, Sports Medicine 49:1923-1947). weight_ref and height_ref: median professional (78 kg, 180 cm). reposition_ticks (3 s), fatigue_coefficient and fatigue_floor: arbitrary, declared, to be sourced at L3. with_ball_share_min and _max (75-95% of the sprint with the ball): order of magnitude, declared, to be sourced at L3.
